entities.name: Nicolaus Ragvaldi
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Nicolaus Ragvaldi, who served as the Archbishop of Uppsala from 1438 until his death in 1448, emerged as a central figure in early 15th-century Swedish ecclesiastical politics and is celebrated as an originator of the influential Gothicist movement. Prior to his elevation to the primacy, he was Bishop of Växjö. His career unfolded during a turbulent period marked by the struggles of the Kalmar Union and the broader conciliar movement within the Catholic Church, positioning him at the nexus of national identity formation and international religious diplomacy in Northern Europe.

Ragvaldi's most enduring contribution stems from his participation in the Council of Basel (1431–1449), where he represented the Swedish church. In a seminal speech delivered on November 12, 1434, he passionately asserted that the Swedes were direct descendants of the Goths, the Germanic people who famously sacked Rome in 410 CE. This assertion, intended to bolster Sweden's standing among European nations and secure its precedence within the Council, laid the intellectual groundwork for what would become known as Gothicism. His tenure as archbishop was also characterized by efforts to consolidate church authority amidst ongoing political instability and conflicts between the Swedish nobility and the Danish monarchy.

The Gothicist tradition, ignited by Ragvaldi's pronouncements at Basel, profoundly shaped Swedish national identity and historiography for centuries. His arguments were later elaborated upon by figures like Johannes Magnus in his 1554 work "Historia de omnibus Gothorum Sveonumque regibus," becoming a cornerstone of Swedish imperial ideology during the 17th century's Age of Greatness. This narrative, though historically contested, provided a powerful cultural and political myth that fueled national pride and justified expansionist ambitions, enduring as a significant element of Swedish self-perception long after its historical accuracy was challenged.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Nicolaus Ragvaldi's articulation of Gothicist ideas at the Council of Basel fundamentally shaped Swedish national identity and historiography for centuries, providing a powerful myth that influenced later imperial ambitions. His actions had a lasting regional impact on Swedish self-perception and political culture.
